direct_answer:
Helleniq integrates sustainability-related performance into incentives through its Board of Directors’ Remuneration Policy and a Long-Term Incentive Plan (LTIP). Variable remuneration is linked to the achievement of group/corporate/individual objectives that include sustainability-related elements (e.g., safety indicators and energy transition progress under “Vision 2025”). For 2024, objectives included quantitative and qualitative targets across safety, competitiveness/efficiency, profitability/financial performance, and progress in the energy transition plan (Vision 2025) [Source 1]. Climate-related considerations are integrated into the variable remuneration structure; performance against targets related to GHG emission reductions is assessed by the Sustainability Committee [Source 2]. Sustainability-related metrics used include safety KPIs (LWIF and AIF accident KPIs) and KPIs related to the Vision 2025 Transformation Plan, including expansion of the RES projects portfolio [Source 2].

For long-term incentives, the Annual General Meeting (27 June 2024) approved an LTIP in the form of a stock award program for senior management and other executives [Source 1][Source 2]. The LTIP has two three-year evaluation cycles with gradual vesting over three years, and share awards require achievement of objectives/KPIs defined by the Board’s Remuneration & Succession Planning Committee [Source 3]. For the 1st evaluation cycle (2024–2026), KPIs are weighted: financial targets 60%, transformation targets 20%, and ESG targets 20% [Source 3]. The Remuneration Policy is approved/updated by the General Meeting of shareholders (approved 20/12/2019; modified 30/06/2021; revised 27/06/2024) [Source 1]. The company states that the percentages of variable remuneration per objective dependent on sustainability-related targets are provided in the latest remuneration report, but those percentages are not included in the retrieved passages [Source 2].
compliance_rationale: The passages describe key characteristics of incentive schemes (Remuneration Policy structure; variable pay linked to objectives; LTIP stock award design and cycles) and identify sustainability-related targets/metrics used (GHG reduction targets assessed by Sustainability Committee; safety KPIs; Vision 2025/RES expansion; ESG targets weighted at 20% in LTIP) and governance approval level (General Meeting; KPIs defined by Remuneration & Succession Planning Committee) [Source 1][Source 2][Source 3]. However, the required proportion of variable remuneration dependent on sustainability targets is only referenced as being in another remuneration report and is not disclosed in the provided evidence [Source 2], limiting full ESRS 2 GOV-3 alignment.
disclosure_gaps: Exact proportion/percentage of variable remuneration dependent on sustainability-related targets/impacts for the administrative, management and supervisory bodies (only referenced as available in the latest remuneration report, not provided in the passages) [Source 2].

Clear mapping of which incentive elements apply specifically to members of the administrative, management and supervisory bodies versus “senior management executives and other executives” (scope is not fully explicit in the passages) [Source 1][Source 2].
Specific sustainability-related targets/thresholds (e.g., numeric GHG reduction targets, safety target levels) used for remuneration outcomes are not detailed in the passages [Source 2].
Whether sustainability performance is assessed against sustainability-related impacts (in addition to targets) is not explicitly described in the passages [Source 2].
key_findings: A Board of Directors’ Remuneration Policy governs fixed/variable remuneration and is approved and revised by shareholder General Meetings (2019 approval; 2021 modification; 2024 revision) [Source 1].
Variable remuneration is linked to annual objectives that include sustainability-related areas such as safety and progress in the energy transition plan (Vision 2025) [Source 1].
Climate-related considerations are integrated into variable remuneration; the Sustainability Committee assesses performance against GHG emission reduction targets [Source 2].
Sustainability-linked KPIs referenced include LWIF and AIF safety KPIs and Vision 2025-related KPIs including expansion of the RES projects portfolio [Source 2].
An LTIP stock award program was approved by the Annual General Meeting (27 June 2024) for senior management and other executives [Source 1][Source 2].
LTIP KPI weightings for 2024–2026 include ESG targets at 20% (financial 60%, transformation 20%, ESG 20%); KPIs are defined by the Board’s Remuneration & Succession Planning Committee [Source 3].
